skill.name: visual-testing-advanced
skill.description: Advanced visual regression testing with pixel-perfect comparison, AI-powered diff analysis, responsive design validation, and cross-browser visual consistency. Use when detecting UI regressions, validating designs, or ensuring visual consistency.

generated_query: We just redesigned our product card component to include a new “add to wishlist” icon and updated the color scheme. Before merging to main, I need to catch any unintended visual shifts across desktop, tablet, and mobile viewports, and verify the change looks consistent in Chrome, Firefox, and Safari. The product card displays dynamic content like user avatars and a live “in stock” counter, so those should be masked during comparison. Can you set up a visual regression suite that captures baseline screenshots of the product card on every viewport and browser, then compares the feature branch against that baseline? I want the final report to clearly mark any real regressions (e.g., layout shifts, font changes) while ignoring minor anti-aliasing differences or dynamic content. The report should be generated in a single HTML file I can share with the team.

edit_instructions.rationale: Without dynamic content masking, the test will incorrectly flag changes in avatars and live counters as regressions, failing the user's need for a focused report on real visual shifts.
Removes AI-powered comparison, causing anti-aliasing differences to be flagged as regressions, violating the user's requirement to ignore minor differences.
Changes the report output from single HTML to JSON, failing the user's explicit request for an HTML file.
The user requires a single HTML report to share with the team; changing the output to PDF fails that requirement.
The user wants to ignore minor anti-aliasing differences; setting threshold to 0 will cause those to be flagged as regressions.
Removes the AI semantic comparison algorithm, so the skill cannot ignore anti-aliasing differences as required by the query.
